facts.fact_text: On 17 August 2010 the applicant notified the Lviv City Mayor on behalf of a local human-rights NGO called 'Vartovi zakonu' of its intention to hold a demonstration every Tuesday from 10.30 a.m. to 1 p.m. near the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office.
The planned demonstration period announced on 17 August 2010 was between 17 August 2010 and 1 January 2011.
The aim of the demonstration announced on 17 August 2010 was to draw attention to the issue of corruption in the prosecution service.
On Tuesday 12 October 2010, further to his previous announcement of 17 August 2010, the applicant informed the Lviv City Council about the demonstration to be held on that particular day.
On 12 October 2010 the applicant organised a peaceful demonstration near the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office between 11.30 a.m. and 12.40 p.m.
About twenty-five persons took part in the demonstration on 12 October 2010 near the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office.
Immediately after the events at the demonstration on 12 October 2010, the applicant was called aside by two police officers.

During the demonstration on 12 October 2010, the demonstrators were standing on the pavement in front of the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office when the police told them that they should remain at a distance of five metres from the building.

The police told the demonstrators that they could not stand on the lawn and should move away, which would have meant standing in the road again and obstructing the traffic, causing temporary traffic-jams.
Immediately after the events at the demonstration on 12 October 2010, the applicant was called aside by two police officers.
The two police officers grabbed the applicant's arms and took him in the direction of the nearby police station.

On 14 October 2010, before taking the applicant to court, the police drew up anew the reports on the administrative offences of malicious disobedience to a lawful order by the police and of breaching the procedure for organising and holding a demonstration.
At 3 p.m. on 14 October 2010 the applicant was taken to the Galytskyy District Court.
By a decision of 14 October 2010, the Galytskyy District Court found the applicant guilty of committing the administrative offence of malicious disobedience to a lawful order by the police.

By a decision of 14 October 2010, the Galytskyy District Court found the applicant guilty of committing the administrative offence of breaching the procedure for organising and holding a demonstration.

The Galytskyy District Court sentenced the applicant to three days of administrative detention starting from 6 p.m. on 14 October 2010, with reference to the relevant provisions of the Code on Administrative Offences.
At around 6 p.m. on 17 October 2010 the applicant was released from administrative detention.

In the reports drawn up on 14 October 2010, the police referred to provisions of the Code on Administrative Offences and to the procedure for organising and holding meetings, rallies, street marches and demonstrations in the city of Lviv.
The Galytskyy District Court noted in its decision of 14 October 2010 that the applicant had held a street march without the permission of the Lviv City Council.

Article 39 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that citizens have the right to assemble peacefully without arms and to hold meetings, rallies, marches and demonstrations, after notifying the executive authorities and bodies of local self-government beforehand.

Article 39 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that restrictions on the exercise of the right to peaceful assembly may be established by a court in accordance with the law, in the interests of national security and public order only, for the purpose of preventing disturbances or crimes, protecting the health of the population, or protecting the rights and freedoms of other persons.

Article 92 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that human and citizens' rights and freedoms, the guarantees of these rights and freedoms, and the main duties of the citizen are determined exclusively by the laws of Ukraine.

Article 185 of the Code on Administrative Offences provides that malicious disobedience to a lawful order or demand by a police officer who is carrying out his official duties shall be punishable by a fine of between eight and fifteen times the minimum monthly wage, or by correctional labour of between one and two months with a deduction of 20% of earnings, or, in the event that in the particular circumstances of the case and with regard to the offender's character these measures are found to be insufficient, by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.

Article 185-1 of the Code on Administrative Offences provides that a breach of the procedure for organising and holding meetings, rallies, street marches and demonstrations shall be punishable by a reprimand or by a fine of between ten and twenty-five times the minimum monthly wage.

Article 185-1 of the Code on Administrative Offences provides that the same actions committed within a year of the application of administrative penalties or by the organiser of the meeting, rally, street procession or demonstration shall be punishable by a fine of between twenty and one hundred times the minimum monthly wage, or by correctional labour of one to two months with a deduction of 20% of earnings, or by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.

The Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 on the procedure for organising and holding meetings, rallies, street marches and demonstrations in the city of Lviv introduced the procedure for organising peaceful gatherings in the city of Lviv.

Item 7 of the procedure introduced by the Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 provided that notification about a planned gathering had to be given at least two working days prior to the date on which it was to be held.

Item 14 of the procedure introduced by the Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 specified that gatherings could not be held in the road (except street marches and demonstrations), on lawns and flower beds, or in front of the central entrance (not closer than seven metres) and other entrances of administrative buildings, nor in case of non-compliance with sanitary norms.

Item 16 of the procedure introduced by the Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 specified that holding a gathering in breach of any of the restrictions imposed by item 14 should be considered a breach of the peace and should engage liability under the law.

In its decision of 19 April 2001, the Constitutional Court of Ukraine noted that the current legislation of Ukraine did not provide for a specific time-limit within which the executive authorities or bodies of local self-government were to be notified about planned meetings, rallies, marches or demonstrations.

In its decision of 19 April 2001, the Constitutional Court of Ukraine held that the provisions of the first part of Article 39 of the Constitution of Ukraine on timely notification to the executive authorities or bodies of local self-government about planned meetings, rallies, marches or demonstrations shall be understood to mean that organisers must inform the authorities in advance, that is, within a reasonable time prior to the date of the planned event.

In its decision of 19 April 2001, the Constitutional Court of Ukraine held that specifying the exact deadlines for timely notification with regard to the particularities of different forms of peaceful assembly, the number of participants, the venue, and the time of the event is a matter for legislative regulation.

In its review of 1 March 2006 on the practice of the Supreme Court of Ukraine in cases concerning administrative offences under Articles 185 to 185-2 of the Code on Administrative Offences, the Supreme Court noted that no legislation had been enacted in Ukraine establishing a mechanism for fulfilling the right to freedom of peaceful assembly.

The information letter of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine of 26 November 2009 noted that the organisation and conduct of peaceful demonstrations is regulated by the Decree of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR of 28 July 1988 No. 9306 on the organisation and holding of meetings, rallies, street marches and demonstrations in the USSR, which is effective in so far as it does not contradict the Constitution of Ukraine pursuant to paragraph 1 of Chapter XV (Transitional Provisions) of the Constitution of Ukraine.

The information letter of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine of 26 November 2009 noted that the requirements as to the organisation and holding of peaceful demonstrations, the time-limit for notification to be given to executive or local government bodies, and the documents to be attached to the application for holding the event are currently not regulated by law.

The information letter of the Ministry of Justice of Ukraine of 26 November 2009 stated that only legislative regulation of the procedure for organising and holding peaceful demonstrations would eliminate the negative practices that had arisen due to the inadequacy of the current state of legal regulation.

During the demonstration on 12 October 2010, the demonstrators were standing on the pavement in front of the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office when the police told them that they should remain at a distance of five metres from the building.
The Galytskyy District Court noted in its decision of 14 October 2010 that the applicant had ignored the lawful demands of the police to stop breaching the peace.

According to the Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004, the freedom of assembly was guaranteed but could be restricted by a court for considerations of public health, prevention of crime and disorder, and protection of the rights of others.

Item 14 of the procedure introduced by the Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 specified that gatherings could not be held in the road (except street marches and demonstrations), on lawns and flower beds, or in front of the central entrance (not closer than seven metres) and other entrances of administrative buildings, nor in case of non-compliance with sanitary norms.

Item 16 of the procedure introduced by the Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 specified that holding a gathering in breach of any of the restrictions imposed by item 14 should be considered a breach of the peace and should engage liability under the law.

On 17 August 2010 the applicant notified the Lviv City Mayor on behalf of a local human-rights NGO called 'Vartovi zakonu' of its intention to hold a demonstration every Tuesday from 10.30 a.m. to 1 p.m. near the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office.
The planned demonstration period announced on 17 August 2010 was between 17 August 2010 and 1 January 2011.
On Tuesday 12 October 2010, further to his previous announcement of 17 August 2010, the applicant informed the Lviv City Council about the demonstration to be held on that particular day.
On 12 October 2010 the applicant organised a peaceful demonstration near the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office between 11.30 a.m. and 12.40 p.m.
About twenty-five persons took part in the demonstration on 12 October 2010 near the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office.
The police's instruction to remain five metres from the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office would have forced the demonstrators to stand in the road and obstruct the traffic.

After some discussion with the police during the demonstration on 12 October 2010, the demonstrators crossed the road and stood on a lawn on the opposite side of the street from the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office.

The police told the demonstrators that they could not stand on the lawn and should move away, which would have meant standing in the road again and obstructing the traffic, causing temporary traffic-jams.

On 13 October 2010 the Lviv Regional Administrative Court granted a request by the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council to prohibit the holding of the pre-announced demonstrations by the applicant's NGO 'Vartovi zakonu' as from 19 October 2010.
The Galytskyy District Court noted in its decision of 14 October 2010 that the applicant had held a street march without the permission of the Lviv City Council.
The Galytskyy District Court noted in its decision of 14 October 2010 that the applicant had ignored the lawful demands of the police to stop breaching the peace.

Having heard the applicant and examined the case-file materials, the Galytskyy District Court concluded that the applicant's testimony was refuted by the written reports of the police officers and the traffic police officers.
The Galytskyy District Court noted in its decision of 14 October 2010 that the police reports had been drawn up correctly and therefore had to be taken into account.

The Galytskyy District Court sentenced the applicant to three days of administrative detention starting from 6 p.m. on 14 October 2010, with reference to the relevant provisions of the Code on Administrative Offences.

In reply to the applicant's arguments that there had been no corpus delicti in his actions, the Lviv Regional Court of Appeal noted in its decision of 27 October 2010 that those arguments should be disregarded because they were refuted by the body of evidence in the case, without elaborating further on that point.
